has_subtypes.description: Bardet-Biedl syndrome caused by biallelic loss-of-function variants in BBS5, which encodes a BBSome subunit. ClinGen curates the gene-disease pair under the broader disease term BBS5-related ciliopathy, whose only MONDO descendant is Bardet-Biedl syndrome 5.

evidence.explanation: States that ClinGen treats BBS5 disease as one gene-level entity, and names the MONDO term this subtype binds.
evidence.snippet: For the purposes of this gene curation, cases caused by biallelic variants in the BBS5 gene have been curated under the broader disease term BBS5-related ciliopathy.

evidence.explanation: Supports loss of function as the variant mechanism the description records.
evidence.snippet: The mechanism of pathogenicity is known to be loss of function.

evidence.explanation: This assembly study places BBS5 among the subunits of the complete BBSome, the basis for describing it as a BBSome subunit.
evidence.reference_title: Intrinsic protein-protein interaction-mediated and chaperonin-assisted sequential assembly of stable bardet-biedl syndrome protein complex, the BBSome.
evidence.snippet: BBS1, BBS5, BBS8, and finally BBS4 are added to the BBSome core to form the complete BBSome.

mondo_mappings.mapping_justification: MONDO places Bardet-Biedl syndrome 5 (OMIM:615983) as the only subclass of BBS5-related ciliopathy, the gene-lumped term ClinGen curates against.

has_subtypes.description: Bardet-Biedl syndrome caused by biallelic loss-of-function variants in BBS7, which encodes a core BBSome subunit. ClinGen curates the gene-disease pair as BBS7-related ciliopathy, a single lumped entity whose only MONDO descendant is Bardet-Biedl syndrome 7. Retinal dystrophy is the most penetrant feature, with the usual BBS extraocular features (obesity, polydactyly, renal abnormalities) varying between patients.

evidence.explanation: ClinGen's evidence summary identifies retinal disease as the most penetrant feature of BBS7 disease, which the description above records.
evidence.snippet: Subsequent publications have established that cases diagnosed with Bardet-Biedl syndrome 7 exhibit retinal disease as the most penetrant feature

evidence.explanation: States why BBS7 disease is one entity, and names the MONDO term this subtype binds.
evidence.snippet: Therefore, cases caused by inherited biallelic BBS7 variants have been lumped into a single disease entity, referred to as BBS7-related ciliopathy.

mondo_mappings.mapping_justification: MONDO places Bardet-Biedl syndrome 7 (OMIM:615984) as the only subclass of BBS7-related ciliopathy, the gene-lumped term ClinGen curates against.

has_subtypes.description: Bardet-Biedl syndrome caused by biallelic BBS10 variants, with loss of function the apparent mechanism. BBS10 encodes a chaperonin-like protein that, with MKKS/BBS6, BBS12 and the CCT/TRiC chaperonins, forms the complex that mediates BBSome assembly. ClinGen lumps syndromic and non-syndromic BBS10 cases into one entity, BBS10-related ciliopathy, whose only MONDO descendant is Bardet-Biedl syndrome 10. All reported cases to date appear to have retinal dystrophy, predominantly rod-cone dystrophy, while the extraocular BBS features vary.

evidence.explanation: States why ClinGen treats syndromic and non-syndromic BBS10 disease as one entity, and names the MONDO term this subtype binds.
evidence.snippet: Because the cases with variable severity of syndromic presentation, including non-syndromic cases (PMID: 36084042), all exhibit a recessive mode of inheritance and share overlapping retinal phenotypes consistent with a single spectrum of disease, these cases have been lumped into a single disease entity, BBS10-related ciliopathy.

evidence.explanation: Supports retinal dystrophy as the constant feature of BBS10 disease.
evidence.snippet: all reported cases to date appear to have retinal dystrophy

evidence.explanation: Supports rod-cone dystrophy as the usual form of the retinal disease.
evidence.snippet: The predominant retinal phenotype is BBS10-related rod-cone dystrophy.

evidence.explanation: Supports loss of function as the apparent variant mechanism, which the description records with the same hedge.
evidence.snippet: The mechanism of pathogenicity appears to be loss of function, as multiple nonsense or frameshift variants resulting in BBS10-related disease are described in the literature

evidence.explanation: Identifies BBS10 as one of the three chaperonin-like BBS proteins whose complex with CCT/TRiC mediates BBSome assembly.
evidence.reference_title: BBS6, BBS10, and BBS12 form a complex with CCT/TRiC family chaperonins and mediate BBSome assembly.
evidence.snippet: Here, we show that a novel complex composed of three chaperonin-like BBS proteins (BBS6, BBS10, and BBS12) and CCT/TRiC family chaperonins mediates BBSome assembly, which transports vesicles to the cilia.

mondo_mappings.mapping_justification: MONDO places Bardet-Biedl syndrome 10 (OMIM:615987) as the only subclass of BBS10-related ciliopathy, the gene-lumped term ClinGen curates against.

has_subtypes.name: BBS10

has_subtypes.description: Bardet-Biedl syndrome caused by biallelic loss-of-function variants in BBS12, which encodes a vertebrate-specific chaperonin-like protein that, with MKKS/BBS6 and BBS10, forms the complex that mediates BBSome assembly. ClinGen curates the gene-disease pair as BBS12-related ciliopathy, whose only MONDO descendant is Bardet-Biedl syndrome 12. Retinal dystrophy is one of its major features, and the other BBS features show variable expressivity.

evidence.explanation: Supports the description of BBS12 as a vertebrate-specific chaperonin-like protein of the BBSome assembly complex.
evidence.snippet: BBS12 encodes a predicted chaperonin-like protein that exists specifically in vertebrates, and forms a complex with BBS6 and BBS10 that functions to mediate the assembly of the BBSome

evidence.explanation: Supports biallelic loss of function as the variant mechanism (the missing hyphen is the source's).
evidence.snippet: The underlying mechanism is biallelic loss-of function variants in the BBS12 gene

evidence.explanation: Supports the variable expressivity of BBS12 disease.
evidence.snippet: Bardet-Biedl syndrome 12 (MIM#: 615989) is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by variable expressivity

evidence.explanation: Names the MONDO term this subtype binds and identifies retinal dystrophy as a major feature.
evidence.snippet: In summary, BBS12 is definitively associated with BBS12-related ciliopathy, in which one of the major features is retinal dystrophy.

mondo_mappings.mapping_justification: MONDO places Bardet-Biedl syndrome 12 (OMIM:615989) as the only subclass of BBS12-related ciliopathy, the gene-lumped term ClinGen curates against.

omimps_mappings.mapping_justification: PS209900 represents the genetically heterogeneous Bardet-Biedl syndrome curated here at the syndrome level. MONDO:0015229 has an exact mapping to this series. The shared ciliary-trafficking mechanism and clinical syndrome support retaining one Disease entry, with gene-specific distinctions recorded within it. This mapping is to the series, not OMIM:209900 (the BBS1 member), and does not assert that every series member has a separately curated subtype or genetic record in this file.
